lessons.title: Submersible Research Drone Depth Sensor
lessons.summary: A marine science club is testing an underwater exploration drone in a tidal lagoon. The drone's vertical sensor reports its position in meters relative to sea level. A reading of zero or higher means the drone is on or above the water surfa

blocks.content:
Question 10 · Page 3.1

Submersible Research Drone Depth Sensor

Program Description

A marine science club is testing an underwater exploration drone in a tidal lagoon. The drone's vertical sensor reports its position in meters relative to sea level. A reading of zero or higher means the drone is on or above the water surface, while a reading below zero means it is submerged underwater. Write a program to check whether the drone is surfaced or submerged based on its depth reading.

Requirements

1. Take an integer input representing the position reading and store it in sensor_reading.
2. If sensor_reading is greater than or equal to 0, print "Surfaced".
3. Otherwise, print "Submerged".

Input

A single integer representing sensor_reading.

Expected Output

Print "Surfaced" if the reading is 0 or greater, otherwise print "Submerged".
Submerged

Sample Input

-5

Constraints

sensor_reading is an integer.

lessons.title: Electric Scooter Battery Gauge Validator
lessons.summary: A smart electric scooter has a digital dashboard display that shows its battery charge level as a percentage. The dashboard computer needs to check if the battery sensor reading is valid and whether the scooter has enough charge for high-sp

blocks.content:
Question 11 · Page 3.2

Electric Scooter Battery Gauge Validator

Program Description

A smart electric scooter has a digital dashboard display that shows its battery charge level as a percentage. The dashboard computer needs to check if the battery sensor reading is valid and whether the scooter has enough charge for high-speed sport mode. Write a program to evaluate the battery charge reading.

Requirements

1. Take an integer input representing the battery percentage and store it in battery_level.
2. If battery_level is less than 0 or greater than 120 (accounting for sensor calibration errors), print "Invalid Reading".
3. If battery_level is greater than or equal to 18, print "Ready to Ride".
4. Otherwise (when the reading is between 0 and 17), print "Low Battery".

Input

A single integer representing battery_level.

Expected Output

- Print "Invalid Reading" if battery_level is less than 0 or greater than 120.
- Print "Ready to Ride" if battery_level is 18 or higher (and not greater than 120).
- Print "Low Battery" otherwise.
Invalid Reading

Sample Input

150

Constraints

battery_level is an integer.

blocks.content:
Question 12 · Page 3.3

Arcade Prize Token Bundler

Program Description

At a gaming arcade, prize tokens can only be redeemed for mystery gift boxes if they are collected in full bundles of 10 tokens. Any loose tokens that do not complete a pack of 10 cannot be redeemed for the box. Write a program to check whether a player's total token count can be formed into complete bundles of 10 with zero tokens left over.

Requirements

1. Take an integer input for the total number of tokens and store it in token_count.
2. Check if token_count is evenly divisible by 10 using the modulus operator (token_count % 10 == 0).
3. If it divides evenly by 10 with no remainder, print "Complete Pack".
4. Otherwise, print "Incomplete Pack".

Input

A single integer representing token_count.

Expected Output

Print "Complete Pack" if token_count is a multiple of 10, otherwise print "Incomplete Pack".
Complete Pack

Sample Input

70

Constraints

token_count >= 0

lessons.title: Space Club Solar System Planet Finder

blocks.content:
Question 13 · Page 3.4

Space Club Solar System Planet Finder

Program Description

In the school astronomy club, members use a computer catalog to identify planets based on their position from the Sun, starting with 1 for the closest planet. Write a program that takes a planet's order number from 1 to 7 and prints the name of the planet.

Rules

1 -> Mercury
2 -> Venus
3 -> Earth
4 -> Mars
5 -> Jupiter
6 -> Saturn
7 -> Uranus

Requirements

1. Take an integer input between 1 and 7 and store it in planet_code.
2. If planet_code is 1, print "Mercury".
3. If planet_code is 2, print "Venus".
4. If planet_code is 3, print "Earth".
5. If planet_code is 4, print "Mars".
6. If planet_code is 5, print "Jupiter".
7. If planet_code is 6, print "Saturn".
8. If planet_code is 7, print "Uranus".

Input

A single integer representing planet_code (from 1 to 7).

Expected Output

The name of the planet corresponding to the entered number.
Venus

Sample Input

2

Constraints

1 <= planet_code <= 7

lessons.title: School Eco-Festival Badge Awarder
lessons.summary: During the annual school eco-festival, students earn activity points by completing green challenges. An automated kiosk awards a digital badge based on how many points a student submits. Write a program to check the student's points and pri

blocks.content:
Question 15 · Page 3.6

School Eco-Festival Badge Awarder

Program Description

During the annual school eco-festival, students earn activity points by completing green challenges. An automated kiosk awards a digital badge based on how many points a student submits. Write a program to check the student's points and print the correct badge name.

Rules

1. If the score is divisible by both 7 and 10, print "EarthHero".
2. If the score is divisible only by 7, print "EcoStar".
3. If the score is divisible only by 10, print "GreenShield".
4. If none of these rules apply, print the original score number.

Requirements

1. Take an integer input for the total points and store it in reward_points.
2. Check if reward_points is divisible by both 7 and 10 (reward_points % 7 == 0 and reward_points % 10 == 0). If true, print "EarthHero".
3. Otherwise, check if reward_points is divisible by 7 (reward_points % 7 == 0). If true, print "EcoStar".
4. Otherwise, check if reward_points is divisible by 10 (reward_points % 10 == 0). If true, print "GreenShield".
5. If none of the conditions match, print the integer value of reward_points.

Input

A single integer representing reward_points.

Expected Output

A string badge name ("EarthHero", "EcoStar", or "GreenShield"), or the original integer if none apply.
EarthHero

Sample Input

70

Constraints

reward_points > 0

blocks.content:
Question 16 · Page 3.7

Youth Coding Club Hardware Grant Waiver

Program Description

A regional STEM education center provides project funding grants for student robotics teams. If a team submits a project proposal with a student leadership rating of 60 or higher out of 100, the center awards a special 10% fee waiver discount on the total hardware kit bill. If the rating is below 60, no fee waiver discount is given. Write a program to calculate the discount amount awarded to the team.

Requirements

1. Take a float input for the hardware kit cost and store it in kit_cost.
2. Take an integer input for the team's leadership score and store it in leadership_score.
3. If leadership_score is greater than or equal to 60, calculate the discount amount as 10% of kit_cost (kit_cost * 0.10).
4. Otherwise, set the discount amount to 0.0.
5. Display the discount amount as a float.

Input

First line: A float representing kit_cost
Second line: An integer representing leadership_score

Expected Output

A single float representing the discount amount.
250.0

Sample Input

2500.0
65

Constraints

kit_cost >= 0.0
leadership_score >= 0

blocks.content:
Question 17 · Page 3.8

Drone Obstacle Course Fastest Lap

Program Description

At the school STEM fair, three students pilot their mini-drones through a timed obstacle course. Each pilot's total run time is recorded in whole seconds. Write a program to find the fastest (smallest) completion time among the three pilots using an if...elif...else structure.

Requirements

1. Take three integer inputs representing the finish times in seconds and store them in time1, time2, and time3.
2. Use an if...elif...else structure to compare the three times and identify the smallest time:
- Check if time1 is less than or equal to both time2 and time3.
- Otherwise, check if time2 is less than or equal to time3.
- Otherwise, identify time3 as the smallest.
3. Print the smallest time value as an integer.

Input

First line: An integer representing time1
Second line: An integer representing time2
Third line: An integer representing time3

Expected Output

A single integer representing the lowest completion time.
18

Sample Input

25
18
30

Constraints

time1 > 0
time2 > 0
time3 > 0

School Sports Club Preference Check

Program Description

During sports club sign-up week, students can vote for their favorite outdoor activity. The club system recognizes votes for either football or badminton in both capitalized and lowercase spellings. Write a program to check the entered sport name and display an encouraging message, or show nothing if any other sport is entered.

2. If sport_choice is "Football" or "football", print:
I choose Football
3. If sport_choice is "Badminton" or "badminton", print:
I choose Badminton
4. For any other input, do not print anything.

Input

A single line containing a string representing sport_choice.

Expected Output

A single line message if the sport matches one of the two choices, otherwise no output.
I choose Football

Sample Input

Football

Constraints

sport_choice contains only alphabetic characters.

School Sports Day Two-Cone Drill Marker Counter

Program Description

During physical education class, the coach sets up an obstacle agility course using numbered checkpoints. At each consecutive checkpoint, the coach places an increasing pair of colored boundary cones (2 cones at the 1st checkpoint, 4 at the 2nd, 6 at the 3rd, and so on). Given the total number of checkpoints n, write a program using a for loop to calculate the total number of cones used across all n checkpoints.

2. Initialize an accumulator variable to keep track of the total cone count.
3. Use a for loop to generate the first n positive even numbers (2, 4, 6, ..., 2*n) and add each number to the total count.
4. Display the final total sum of cones as an integer.

Input

A single integer representing n.

Expected Output

A single integer representing the sum of the first n even numbers.
30

Constraints

lessons.title: Cyber Club Secret Passcode Security Validator
lessons.summary: In a school cybersecurity workshop, students design a digital safe that opens only with special "unbreakable" passcodes. An unbreakable passcode is a positive whole number greater than 1 that cannot be split evenly into equal groups by any

blocks.content:
Question 22 · Page 3.13

Cyber Club Secret Passcode Security Validator

Program Description

In a school cybersecurity workshop, students design a digital safe that opens only with special "unbreakable" passcodes. An unbreakable passcode is a positive whole number greater than 1 that cannot be split evenly into equal groups by any number other than 1 and itself (a prime number). Write a program that uses a flag variable to determine whether an entered passcode number is unbreakable (prime) or breakable (not prime).

Requirements

1. Take an integer input for the passcode number and store it in passcode.
2. Initialize an integer variable named flag to 0.
3. Use a loop that starts at 2 and runs up to passcode - 1:
- In each step, check if passcode divides evenly by the current loop number (using the modulus operator %).
- If it divides evenly with a remainder of 0, change the value of flag to 1.
4. After the loop finishes, check the value of flag:
- If flag is equal to 1, print "Breakable Code".
- Otherwise, print "Unbreakable Code".

Input

A single integer representing passcode (where passcode > 1).

Expected Output

Print "Unbreakable Code" if the number is prime, or "Breakable Code" if it is divisible by any number in the range.
Unbreakable Code

Sample Input

7

Constraints

passcode > 1

blocks.content:
Question 23 · Page 3.14

Amusement Park Ticket Serial Code Length Checker

Program Description

At a theme park, game booths scan serial code numbers printed on student ride tickets. The scanner computer needs to count how many digits are in the ticket code using repeated division so it can verify the ticket format. Write a program using a while loop to count and display the total number of digits in the serial code.

Requirements

1. Take a positive integer input for the ticket code and store it in serial_code.
2. Create an integer variable named digit_count and give it a starting value of 0.
3. Use a while loop that keeps running as long as serial_code is not equal to 0.
4. Inside the loop:
- Divide serial_code by 10 using integer division (//) to remove its last digit in each step.
- Increase digit_count by 1.
5. After the loop stops, print the final value of digit_count.

Input

A single positive integer representing serial_code.

Expected Output

A single integer representing the total number of digits in the entered number.
3

Sample Input

556

Constraints

serial_code > 0

Track and Field Yellow Hurdle Station Locator

Program Description

During the school sports day obstacle course, numbered hurdles are arranged in a straight lane from station 1 to station n. Only the odd-numbered hurdles are painted bright yellow for a special jumping relay, while all even-numbered hurdles are skipped. Write a program using a loop to find and display all the yellow hurdle station numbers from 1 to n.

Requirements

1. Take an integer input for the total number of hurdle stations and store it in total_hurdles.
2. Run a loop that goes through each station number from 1 to total_hurdles.
3. Check if the current station number is even (divisible by 2). If it is even, skip it.
4. Print each odd-numbered station on a new line.

Input

A single integer representing total_hurdles.

Expected Output

A sequence of integers, each on a new line, showing all odd numbers from 1 up to total_hurdles.
1
3
5
7
9

10

Constraints

total_hurdles >= 1

blocks.content:
Question 25 · Page 3.16

School Reading Marathon Minute Logger

Program Description

During the school reading challenge, students log the number of minutes they spend reading each book chapter. To finish entering their daily log and exit the recording system, they enter a negative number (such as -1) as a stop signal. Write a program using a while True loop to display all valid reading minute entries, stopping immediately without printing the negative exit number.

Requirements

1. Run a while loop that is always True (while True).
2. Inside the loop, take an integer input and store it in reading_minutes.
3. If reading_minutes is less than 0 (a negative number), stop and exit the loop immediately using a break statement.
4. Otherwise, print the value of reading_minutes.
5. Make sure the negative exit number is never printed.

Input

A series of integers entered one per line, ending with a negative integer.

Expected Output

Each valid non-negative integer printed on a separate line. The negative number must not appear in the output.
10
25
7

Sample Input

10
25
7
-1

Constraints

Valid reading entries are integers >= 0.
The loop stops on the first integer < 0.

lessons.title: Sports Equipment Paired Item Scanner
lessons.summary: During after-school sports cleanup, a student helper scans batches of training items (such as shuttlecocks, tennis balls, and wristbands) into the inventory system. The system only logs batches that can be split evenly into pairs (even numb

blocks.content:
Question 26 · Page 3.17

Sports Equipment Paired Item Scanner

Program Description

During after-school sports cleanup, a student helper scans batches of training items (such as shuttlecocks, tennis balls, and wristbands) into the inventory system. The system only logs batches that can be split evenly into pairs (even numbers). If a student enters an odd quantity, the scanner skips it. When the helper enters 0, the scanning session ends completely. Write a program using a while True loop to print only the even batch counts until 0 is entered.

Requirements

1. Run a loop that repeats indefinitely (while True).
2. Take an integer input on each pass and store it in item_count.
3. If item_count is equal to 0, stop and exit the loop immediately using a break statement.
4. If item_count is odd (item_count % 2 != 0), skip the rest of the loop step using a continue statement.
5. If item_count is even and not 0, print the value of item_count.

Input

A series of integers entered one per line, ending with 0.

Expected Output

Only the even integers printed on separate lines. Odd numbers and the sentinel value 0 must not be printed.
12
8
10

Sample Input

12
7
8
5
10
0

Constraints

Inputs are non-negative integers.
The program terminates when item_count is 0.

Botany Club Sunflower Spiral Counter

Write a program using a loop to display the first n numbers of this spiral sequence.
